agent_note: Prose fiction, not verse. Two clear first-person voices: a modern narrator ('I clench my teeth', 'I shush my mind') and a child narrator (q01499 'I hold Huckleberry Finn real tight against my chest and start across the yard'), both narrating in present tense. A third dialect voice appears in q01462/q01467/q01479. Past-tense event quotes are all retrospective/summary material inside a present base (q01493 'We didn't have fancy dresses', q01484, q01463, q01459), i.e. a recollection strand rather than a second narrating position. Heavy gnomic load (20 of 47) -- this book's Goodreads page is dominated by inspirational aphorisms, exactly the contamination the gnomic bucket exists for. Two paratext quotes (dedication q01468, acknowledgments q01475).
